decisive_items: a 34×28 mm sacrococcygeal mass with internal and external components
a 60×70×57 mm sacrococcygeal mass with mixed features—predominantly solid with a 40 mm cyst—and no invasion or compression of pelvic structures or the coccyx (Altman type II)
response.rationale: The vignette is centered on a prenatally detected sacrococcygeal mass with characteristic imaging features, making sacrococcygeal teratoma the primary diagnosis; the bleeding and shock are complications of this mass.

rejected.why: Neonatal hemorrhagic shock is a downstream complication of active bleeding from the sacrococcygeal mass, not the underlying most likely diagnosis.
Respiratory distress syndrome is nonspecific and reflects prematurity/resuscitation needs rather than the defining sacrococcygeal pathology.
